technical_sources.supports: The architecture began with explicit ownership and failure boundaries.
Hardware eligibility became composable and evidence-backed.
A deterministic virtual receiver graph separated software proof from physical assurance.
The product constitution defines the bridge mission and non-ownership boundaries.
The release inventory is capability-based rather than a local serial or port allowlist.
The bridge protocol became a generated and versioned SDK contract.
The kernel interface was reduced to a stable bounded UAPI.
Receiver transport entered the kernel with bounded I/O and preserved input ownership.
Native receiver exchange was generalized without device-instance branches.
Protocol versions one through seven remain explicit compatibility surfaces.
Kernel operations and versions remain canonical and fixed-width.
Lifecycle and transaction authority became explicit core state machines.
Stable restoration records became crash-safe and durable.
Receiver generations became an atomic bridge orchestration boundary.
Stale-profile restoration work was suppressed before claim creation.
Protected behavior and known evidence gaps are explicit release inputs.
Persistence, locking, and restoration failure semantics are documented separately from normal operation.
OpenRGB integration began from a pinned adapter boundary.
Canonical controllers were adapted to the stock OpenRGB native API.
The OpenRazer route was implemented as a source-bound native relay.
The OpenRGB route became source-bound without replacing the application.
Private application takeover boundaries were removed.
The exact two-package Pacman transition was qualified.
Stock application ownership and connector boundaries are canonical.
The OpenRazer adaptation remains pinned to reviewed upstream source.
The packaged plugin transform records accepted and rejected upstream behavior.
Verification began emitting source-bound run evidence.
Hardware lifecycle qualification acquired explicit supervision and stop gates.
Native parity gained a bounded read-only qualifier.
Relay publication was gated by stable source-derived serial identity.
Release eight became the accepted private behavioral reference.
The accepted installed baseline separates machine evidence, operator observations, and limitations.
Release and publication authority remain separate from passing tests.
The installed release eight baseline was sealed before reconstruction.
Every 2.0 source disposition entered an auditable reconstruction ledger.
The lean Core and integration-complete Full boundary became canonical.
Embedded subsystem tests were extracted without changing public behavior.
Large-module dispositions became explicit Phase 4 evidence.
Quality, security, and measured optimization received a bounded audit.
The private journey extraction scope became fail-closed and product-specific.
The reconstruction ledger records every keep, move, split, and retirement decision.
The Phase 5 audit records quality, security, dependency, and performance outcomes.
